_network_type: Nested leave-one-speaker-out (LOSO/LOGO) architecture search: NSGA-II runs SEPARATELY for each of 4 model families (SNN-AE, LSTM-AE, GRU-AE, Transformer-AE), one OS process per (dataset, outer fold). Goal (2026-09-22 scope change): find the best autoencoder overall across all 4 families at equal latent_dim WITHIN a dataset, not 'SNN vs 3 fixed baselines' -- every family now searches its own architecture and its own input encoding. latent_dim itself is per-dataset since 2026-09-23 (see dataset.sources[].latent_dim): audio (fsdd/audiomnist) and EEG (eegmmidb/chbmit) use different bottleneck widths, literature-backed -- .wiki/Experiments/Meeting01.md's 'latent_dim is fixed, not evolved' section has the citations.
_architecture_summary: SNN-AE: free encoder_widths genome (strictly decreasing, decoder mirrors encoder), exponential surrogate; R, C, V_th learnable, clamped 1e-6. LSTM-AE/GRU-AE: hidden_size + num_layers genes (Meeting01RecurrentGaGenome). Transformer-AE: d_model + n_heads + n_layers + d_ff genes, d_model % n_heads == 0 enforced by repair (Meeting01TransformerGaGenome). All 4: encoding (direct/poisson/latency) is a gene, latent_dim is fixed per dataset (never a gene) so every family is compared at the same compression ratio within that dataset -- fsdd/audiomnist (audio) = 16, eegmmidb/chbmit (EEG) = 64 (dataset.sources[].latent_dim, resolved once per dataset before that dataset's 4 searches start). Each family's driver runs its own NSGA-II (population x (1+generations) evaluations), selects the winning genome from its own rank-0 Pareto front on the inner validation speaker, retrains it on train+val (early-stopping on a recording-disjoint monitor carved from train), evaluates once on the held-out test speaker, then the 4 winners are compared (val_mse, then inference cost) and the overall winner is recorded in a '_run<r>_overall_winner_manifest.json'.
_preprocessing: Non-overlapping 256-sample windows (32 ms @ 8 kHz for FSDD / AudioMNIST; 1.6 s @ 160 Hz for PhysioNet eegmmidb; 1 s @ 256 Hz for CHB-MIT). Per-window z-score, then spike encoding over model.time_steps = 16 REAL simulation steps -> a (16, 256) time-major tensor (row = t*B + b). Encoding (direct/poisson/latency) is a GA gene for every family, not an outer sweep. Every model -- SNN and the three baselines alike -- is trained to reconstruct the ORIGINAL z-scored window (repeated across the 16 steps), never its own spike code, so val_mse is comparable across encodings and families. Stratified per-fold window caps (loso_max_{train,val,test}_windows = 200 / 150 / 1500) round-robin across recording_id so every speaker/recording stays represented; LOSO structure and the recording-level statistical unit are unchanged.
_total_runs_breakdown: Per (dataset, fold, run_id): 4 SEPARATE NSGA-II searches (SNN + LSTM + GRU + Transformer), each population x (1 + generations) evaluations + |Pareto front| x (winner_seeds - 1) re-scorings + 1 retrained winner. CALIBRATED 2026-09-23 from a real per-epoch cost probe at production settings (window_size=256, time_steps=16, 200 train / 150 val windows, batch_size=1, each family pinned to a production-representative genome: SNN 64->32, LSTM/GRU hidden=64, Transformer d_model=64/heads=4/layers=2/d_ff=128). Measured mean wall-clock per epoch: SNN ~0.5 s, Transformer ~83.75 s (168x SNN), LSTM ~97.2 s (194x SNN), GRU ~136.0 s (272x SNN). At these ratios a literal equal-wall-clock-to-SNN budget (SNN's own 48 evaluations cost only ~12 min worst-case) is mathematically incompatible with running any real search on the 3 baseline families, so the equal-TIME-budget design (as originally conceived) was abandoned for them (user decision, 2026-09-23) in favor of each getting its own independently-sized evaluation budget. ga.lstm/ga.gru/ga.transformer are set to population=8, generations=5, winner_seeds=3 -- the SAME shape as ga.snn (48 search evaluations each, user's explicit choice after seeing the per-family cost breakdown, deliberately prioritizing search thoroughness over minimizing wall-clock). 65 evaluations per family per cell worst case (48 search + up to |front|x2=16 winner's-curse re-scorings + 1 final retrain). Worst-case total (every evaluation running the full 30-epoch cap, no early stop) per (dataset,fold,run) cell: SNN ~0.27 h, Transformer ~45.4 h, LSTM ~52.7 h, GRU ~73.7 h -- summing to ~172 h/cell (cited, not recomputed, from the 2026-09-23 measurement). Grid widened 2026-09-23 from 3 to 4 datasets (mitbih replaced by two EEG datasets, eegmmidb + chbmit, per user request) -- per-cell cost is unchanged, so the prior 90-cell total (~15 476 CPU-hours) scales by 120/90: across the full grid (4 datasets x 6 folds x 5 repeats = 120 cells): approximately 20 635 CPU-hours, i.e. ~860 days (~28.7 months) WORST CASE. Real elapsed time will be lower thanks to early_stop_patience=5 truncating most evaluations well before 30 epochs, but no measured average-epochs-under-early-stopping exists yet -- this is a stated upper bound, not a point estimate. Confirm cluster/wall-clock capacity for a job of this scale before launching; consider splitting across (dataset, fold) processes run in parallel (already the design -- one OS process per cell) to bring elapsed wall-clock down, though total CPU-hours are unchanged.
_dataset_config: Speaker/record-disjoint outer folds (6). No pooled sample caps (max_loaded_train_samples / max_validation_samples = 0 -> every window of the disjoint partitions, then the stratified loso_max_* caps apply). 30 epochs max, early stop patience 5, lr 0.001 (weights) / 0.0001 (R, C, V_th), batch size 1. Per-epoch progress on stderr as '[loso] ... epoch N/M' (survives nohup, where the live bars collapse).
_comment: Nested-LOSO multi-family architecture search for the meeting01 paper revision. GA budgets for all 4 families are calibrated from a real per-epoch cost measurement (2026-09-23) -- see _total_runs_breakdown for the method. ga.lstm/ga.gru/ga.transformer match ga.snn's own shape (population=8, generations=5, winner_seeds=3, 48 search evaluations each -- user's explicit choice, 2026-09-23, after being shown the per-family cost breakdown). Dataset grid changed 2026-09-23: mitbih (ECG) replaced by two EEG datasets, eegmmidb + chbmit (user request), both read via a new EDF-format loader (Meeting01Eeg.{hpp,cpp}) -- see dataset.sources[] for the (currently PLACEHOLDER) root paths, not yet downloaded on this machine. Worst-case grid estimate, updated for 4 datasets: ~860 days (~28.7 months) of CPU time (cited, scaled from the 3-dataset ~645-day estimate -- see _total_runs_breakdown). Run once via scripts/pipeline/meeting01/01_meeting01_run_loso.sh (ONE invocation; potentially close to THREE YEARS on CPU worst case -- confirm cluster capacity and timeline before launching). cv_fold here is a default; the run script overrides it per process with --cv-fold.

sources.name: fsdd
sources._latent_dim_comment: 16 (16:1 vs the 256-sample window): short-speech/traditional AE and LSTM bottlenecks in the literature sit at 8-16 -- see .wiki/Experiments/Meeting01.md.

sources.name: audiomnist
sources._latent_dim_comment: 16 (16:1): same short-speech domain as fsdd; AudioMNIST encoders in the literature sit in the 16-64 range -- see .wiki/Experiments/Meeting01.md.

sources._comment: PLACEHOLDER path -- dataset not yet downloaded on this machine (2026-09-23). Source: PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, https://physionet.org/content/eegmmidb/1.0.0/ (109 subjects, 64 channels, 160 Hz, EDF+, one subdirectory per subject: S001/S001R01.edf ...). Signal 0 of each .edf is read; verify that is an EEG channel (not e.g. a status channel) once the real files are in place.
sources.name: eegmmidb
sources._latent_dim_comment: 64 (4:1): no eegmmidb-specific AE paper found; extrapolated from CHB-MIT (same EEG modality/window scale) -- see .wiki/Experiments/Meeting01.md.

sources._comment: PLACEHOLDER path -- dataset not yet downloaded on this machine (2026-09-23). Source: CHB-MIT Scalp EEG Database, https://physionet.org/content/chbmit/1.0.0/ (22 subjects, up to 23 channels, 256 Hz, EDF, one subdirectory per subject: chb01/chb01_01.edf ...). Signal 0 of each .edf is read; verify that is an EEG channel once the real files are in place.
sources.name: chbmit
sources._latent_dim_comment: 64 (4:1): Khan et al. 2023 (shallow AE, CHB-MIT) use hidden_size=64; a separate {32,64,128} sweep on CHB-MIT also picked 64 -- see .wiki/Experiments/Meeting01.md.

model._latent_dim_comment: Fallback only: every dataset in evaluation.datasets below overrides this via dataset.sources[].latent_dim (16 audio / 64 EEG), so this value is never actually read by the LOSO grid -- kept as a sane default for ad-hoc single-dataset runs of this profile with --dataset omitted-override.
